PASS on the fake backend only (evidence contract_checked, never an MHS-Device level); this package is model-authored and unreviewed (driver.lock.json reviewed_by is null), no hardware was attached or run, and no hardware or sim-engine run is claimed. The card's entry_symbols is empty, so there was no entry symbol to verify; the card's two models exist in the clone (scene.xml:1 and g1.xml:1). The package serves the card's models[0], scene.xml, as a configuration-only MujocoDriver in simulated R0 mode. cap.world.step.v1 takes {ticks, action: {ctrl: [43 numbers]}}; the 29 body position actuators are in default class g1, whose position default sets inheritrange 1 (g1.xml:9-10), so each body control range is the matching joint range (g1.xml:93-382). The 14 finger actuators have no class, ctrlrange or inheritrange (g1.xml:435-449), and their joints have explicit ranges (g1.xml:254-289,347-382); the package's fake stand-in applies the matching joint range as a conservative deployment envelope, so the fake's contract has one 43-element control interval. The real MJCF leaves those 14 control elements unbounded; the stand-in envelope is not a ctrlrange the MJCF states, and the fidelity gaps say so. DEVIATION FROM THE CARD: the family stays configuration-only except for the package's FiniteCtrlLimitsBridge.action_limits override, which keeps the fake's single finite 43-element interval and, on a real MuJoCo model with mixed finite and sentinel ranges, publishes only the finite ranges as scalar limit paths; the stock bridge represents an actuator with no ctrlrange by [-sys.float_info.max, +sys.float_info.max], which is not a bound the model states (and the gate would probe it as one). The card's MujocoDriver helper still serves the device; the decision and helper were not changed. cap.world.reset.v1 runs mj_resetData/mj_forward and returns the model defaults; the world state is {time_ms, qpos, qvel, ctrl, tick, timestep_ms, seed}, with 57 qpos and 55 qvel (two free joints and 43 hinge joints) and 43 ctrl values. The served step is the MJCF's own 0.005 s (g1.xml:4; run.py:527), the fidelity is F1 with lockstep clock and realtime_factor 0, and snapshot_restore is the bridge's fallback (the stand-in does not implement mj_getState/mj_setState).

WHY THIS SHAPE: the card is family-config with helper MujocoDriver and the upstream provides a MuJoCo scene with MJCF models rather than a device class, so the family expresses the interface. The fake is a stand-in for the mujoco library, not MuJoCo; it parses the scene and g1.xml include for the joint layout, the actuator list, the control ranges and the 0.005 s option, but its integration is a placeholder first-order motion; it loads no mesh or texture, resolves no contact, gravity, damping, joint limit, force limit, sensor or camera, and the red cylinder's free joint never falls or rolls. MuJoCo was not importable where the gate ran, so no trajectory was compared with the real engine and the sim backend (real mujoco) was not run.

NOT COVERED: the RGB camera images (head_cam, wrist_cam, overhead, side_view, tracking), the ONNX walker, croucher, rotator and right-reacher policies, the keyboard controller, the grip toggle and the model_config.json action scales; cap.world.step.v1 and [...]
